See the formula ↓

How the calculation works

Replacement: (Current GPA × Credits + (New − Old) × Course credits) ÷ Credits

A worked example

A 3.00 GPA over 30 credits includes a 3-credit course scored at 2.00 points. Replacing it with 4.00 adds six quality points, giving 96/30 = 3.20. Counting both attempts instead gives (90 + 12) ÷ 33 = 3.09.

Before you use the result

The current GPA must already include the original course. Both attempts must have the same credit value and scale. This tool applies your selected policy as a scenario; it does not determine your school’s actual retake eligibility, limits or transcript rules. Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

Which policy should I choose?

Check your registrar’s rules. Do not assume that a repeated course removes the original grade.

Does earned degree credit double when both attempts count?

Not necessarily. GPA-bearing attempted credits and credits earned toward graduation can be different totals.
